title: CFC-12 and SF6 allow zero mean-age change in 89 matched section bins on sigma0 26.5
abstract: We test whether repeated CFC-12 and SF6 values require older mean water on sigma0 26.5. We use published GLODAPv2.2023 bins on A20, A22, P02 and P16N and linear programs over nonnegative age distributions. With ages from 0 to 200 years, full surface saturation and a two-percent tracer tolerance with stated floors, all 89 feasible matched endpoint bins allow zero mean-age change. One further bin cannot fit the tracer constraints. Only 44 of 89 permit one unchanged full distribution. Line-mean age-change bounds include zero on all four lines, also with a 100-year age limit. Near-exact tracer fits retain the zero-change result. Over all occupations, 71 of 76 feasible bins permit a common mean, but only 19 permit one common distribution; five North Atlantic bins require local mean variation. These are discrete feasible-set bounds, not confidence intervals. They do not impose a common circulation or a time-evolution law. The result extends earlier model bias tests to the actual tracer values. It separates evidence of distribution change from evidence of older mean water and supports testing ventilation models against tracer concentrations rather than one assumed mean age. It does not reject outcrop-driven oxygen loss. Code, aggregate results, input hashes and an external-scratch reproduction script are included.

display.caption: Finite-grid mean-age-change bounds and separate tests of a common age distribution. Bounds are conditional feasible ranges, not confidence intervals.
